A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AUTOGRAPH study. All 39 pages, including Appendices A–F, figures, tables, equations, and the checklist, support comparison after matching relocated material and renumbered tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original AUTOGRAPH experiments on synthetic, large-graph, and molecular generation benchmarks, including transfer, conditional generation, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results and reports an additional qualitative finding about semantic failures during unconstrained decoding of attributed graphs.

M1.justification: SENT sampling, tokenization, architectures, and the training objective are unchanged. Both versions already describe constrained decoding; v3 revises its reported experimental use without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: The same Planar, SBM, Proteins, Point Clouds, QM9, MOSES, and GuacaMol benchmarks, NetworkX and PubChem-10M pretraining data, and motif-conditioned generation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding synthetic, large-graph, molecular, and timing comparisons. ANFM is newly cited in related work but is not added to the evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 revises the reported decoding setting: v2 says no experiments used transition constraints, whereas v3 specifies constrained decoding for all molecular experiments and unconstrained decoding for unattributed graphs. This is a reported protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 revises the existing constrained-versus-unconstrained decoding comparison by distinguishing graph types and reporting semantic failures on attributed graphs. The other architecture, sampling, representation, model-size, transfer, and motif analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix F.1 retains evaluation sampling with ten different seeds for DiGress, ESGG, and AUTOGRAPH, together with the same error-bar reporting in Table 11. No statistical procedure or run-count disclosure changes.

E6.justification: Appendix C.3 replaces the unqualified finding that unconstrained decoding always produced semantically correct sequences with a finding restricted to unattributed graphs, adding possible failures on attributed graphs. Numerical results, plotted findings, and generated examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, tokenization formulas, complexity reasoning, and theoretical results are unchanged, including Theorems 2.5, 2.14, and 2.15 and their Appendix D proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about graph-to-sequence modeling, scalability, benchmark performance, transfer, and substructure-conditioned generation without fine-tuning.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 narrows the applicability of unconstrained decoding and newly recommends constrained decoding for attributed and complex graphs. This qualifies v2's broad statement that constraints were unnecessary; the other interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 now specifies which graph experiments used constrained decoding, revising the earlier blanket description. The constraint mechanism itself, Appendix E implementation and hardware details, hyperparameters, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds five works covering ANFM, Structure-aware Transformer, GraphiT, LLAGA, and Talk Like a Graph. Brief additions acknowledge filtration-based generation, random-walk features in transformers, and graph representations for LLM understanding without substantially redefining the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized prose changes in related work, Appendix C.3, and acknowledgements. The unchanged checklist moves from after the appendices to before them; the main narrative and scientific section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The timing table moves from page 7, Table 2, to page 8, Table 3; the Proteins/Point Clouds comparison becomes Table 2. Text and floats reflow, and appendix pages relocate, while figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility and interpretive precision by replacing v2's unqualified decoding description with explicit molecular inference settings and a stated failure boundary in Appendix C.3. The added related work also improves context. These gains are limited because the method, quantitative evidence, and theoretical results remain unchanged.
